statement: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, and then in half again, to make a smaller square. The corner where the two folds meet is cut off with one straight cut, and one hole is punched through the middle of the small square. How many holes are in the paper when it is unfolded?

choices.misconception: I counted one hole from the cut and one from the punch, without thinking about the layers.
I thought two folds make only two layers, so the punch made 2 holes, plus 1 from the cut.
I thought cutting a corner only makes a notch, so I counted just the 4 punched holes.
I thought the cut corner makes 4 holes as well, one in each layer, like the punch.

hints: How many layers thick is the folded square?
Folding twice makes four layers, so a punch through the middle goes through all four. The folded corner, though, is the centre of the big sheet, where all four layers meet at one point.
The punch makes 4 holes, one in each quarter. The four cut corners all meet at the centre and join into a single hole.

solutions.reliable: Two folds make four layers, so the punch makes 4 holes, one in each quarter of the sheet. The corner where both folds meet is the centre of the original square. Cutting it off removes a small triangle from each of the four layers, and those four triangles fit together around the centre into one diamond-shaped hole. So there are 4 + 1 = 5 holes. The transferable idea: unfold step by step and track where each cut sits on the original sheet; cuts on a fold join up across it instead of making separate holes.

whyOnTest: Folding and punching tests tracking layers, and noticing that a cut on the folds joins into one hole instead of several.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
